claim: KB.1 note 9 research claims (pseudo-thinking vs real reasoning): (1) CoT benefits are scale-emergent — <100B models get no positive gain from CoT prompting, smaller models produce fluent but illogical chains (Wei et al., NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2201.11903); (2) implicit post-hoc rationalization exists on realistic prompts with production-model rates 0.04%-13% (Sonnet 3.7 thinking 0.04%, DeepSeek R1 0.37%, GPT-4o-mini 13%; arXiv:2503.08679v4); (3) flip-pair introspective faithfulness: surface reasoning text retains 96% same-answer similarity (cosine 0.784 vs 0.817), true self-knowledge signal is in the confidence layer (r=0.134, p<0.001; arXiv:2605.27773v1); (4) test-time compute scaling requires verification signals to be asymptotically optimal (VB > VF; Setlur et al., arXiv:2502.12118, empirical on 3/8/32B); (5) excessive CoT length impairs performance (overthinking, Thinking-Optimal Scaling, OpenReview 6ICFqmixlS); (6) no single TTS strategy universally dominates across 8 open-source LLMs 7B-235B (Agarwal et al., arXiv:2512.02008); (7) smaller model + advanced inference (tree search) can Pareto-dominate larger model (Llemma-7B+tree search > Llemma-34B on MATH, ICLR 2025). Please adversarially review: which claims are unsupported, misattributed, or overgeneralized? Are the cited numbers accurate?
